approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would take money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund to pay for the government's everyday running costs.
It would provide about seven-twelfths of the estimated annual funding for the 2016-2017 financial year, plus full-year budget measures.
A separate bill, Supply Bill (No. 1) 2016-2017, would cover the remaining five-twelfths to ensure enough money for the first part of the year.
Proposes appropriations from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for ordinary annual services.
Sets the appropriation at seven-twelfths of estimated annual funding plus full-year budget measures.
Works with Supply Bill (No. 1) 2016-2017 to cover the residual five-twelfths.
The government and its departments that receive ordinary annual services funding.

The Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2016-2017 seeks just under $9 billion for non‑ordinary annual services, including $4.9 billion for the National Broadband Network, $1.4 billion for defence (with an additional $700 million for the 2016 defence white paper), $544 million for infrastructure programs such as Roads to Recovery and Western Sydney airport, and $310 million for agriculture, including a $50 million national water infrastructure loan facility.
